description: Heat Roadmap Europe (HRE) is a series of studies since 2012, led from Aalborg University, that has produced more than 50 reports and datasets on low-carbon heating and cooling in Europe. The site, read on 2026-09-26, says the latest edition HRE4, funded under EU Horizon 2020 grant 695989, built roadmaps for 14 member states that account for 80 percent of heating and cooling demand. The demand profile page offers 2015 heating and cooling profiles by sub-sector and energy carrier, country presentations for the 14 countries, and Excel spreadsheets for all EU28 member states. The maps page presents the Pan-European Thermal Atlas (Peta4), a free web map for the 14 HRE4 countries with modelled heat demand density, 100 m cooling demand density, district heating areas, prospective supply districts, excess heat sources including metro stations and waste water plants, geothermal potential and recommended district heating levels in version 4.3. Energy models and reports are also listed. No licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: the latest news dates from 2021, so data reflect 2015 conditions and HRE4 scenarios. Simulation uses are district heating potential for capacity planning and heat supply optimisation. Related records: data-seenergies-open-data-hub republishes thermal atlas layers.
